newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee on tightrope v dlr, propped by RBI.
newsitem.headline: India rupee on tightrope v dlr, propped by RBI.

text.p: The rupee ended Thursday at 35.6950/7025, continuing its tight-rope walk against the dollar as the central bank continued to prop up the U.S. currency for the sixth successive trading day, dealers said.
"They bought at the 35.70-level today also," said the chief dealer at a leading public sector bank. The intervention came after the rupee breached the 35.70-mark to trade briefly at 35.6975, he said.
The RBI intervention came a few minutes before the market closed in what dealers now describe as 'typical RBI style.'
Many banks refrained from aggressive dollar selling on Thursday in anticipation of RBI's entry, some dealers said.
"But no one had a speculative position today...people were not long (on dollars) either," said a foreign bank dealer.

A dealer at a foreign bank said he would not describe the RBI action as an intervention. "Banks went to him and sold dollars," he said. This went largely unnoticed, depriving some banks of an opportunity to sell to the RBI, another dealer said.
The morning session saw deals at 35.7075 rupees.

The State Bank of India (SBI), India's largest bank, absorbed a sizeable quantity of dollars, again without active bidding, a dealer said. "A lot of people went and sold to him at 35.7050 level," he said.
The forward dollar market was relatively calm. The six-month annualised premium closed at 3.52 percent compared with the previous close of 3.53 percent, dealers said.

Some dealers said the observation of securities firm SocGen Crosby economist, who told Reuters Financial Television on Wednesday that RBI was going easy on money supply with a view to cap the rupee's rise, appeared to ring true.
"They have been buying dollars every day this week," a dealer said about RBI's dollar purchases.
The RBI bought dollars this week at a price range of 35.70 to 35.73.
